root_cause.text: The fprop_new_period() function used preempt_disable_nested() to protect the write side of the sequence counter, which does not disable hardirqs, allowing a hardirq to interrupt while the seqcount is in write state and causing a deadlock when the hardirq handler tries to read the same seqcount.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message detail the race: after write_seqcount_begin(&p->sequence), a hardirq triggers blk_mq_end_request() which eventually calls fprop_fraction_percpu() to read the seqcount, and seeing an odd sequence (write in progress) causes an indefinite loop. The patch replaces preempt_disable_nested() with local_irq_save()/local_irq_restore() to make the write section hardirq-safe.
